title: Aft Fuselage Frame Foot — Material Loss Blend-Out and Spliced Renewal
abstract: Permanent repair for corrosion material loss at the frame foot in the aft bilge, covering blend-out inside the allowable depth and, beyond it, a cut-back and spliced renewal with an attached inspection requirement.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the residual fatigue capability of an aft fuselage frame foot after corrosion material loss, either by blending the loss out or by cutting the foot back and splicing in new material.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the loss by the ultrasonic grid measurement of the applicable inspection task, at 25 mm spacing along the foot. Record the minimum remaining thickness at every grid point. Loss up to 12 per cent of nominal thickness, not extending into the foot radius and not closer than 20 mm to a fastener centre, may be blended out and re-protected under this repair. Loss between 12 and 25 per cent, or loss that reaches the radius, requires the cut-back and splice. Loss above 25 per cent, loss at more than three consecutive frame stations, or any loss that crosses the shear tie footprint is outside this repair and needs an engineering assessment. Record the position of every finding against the frame station before any material is removed.
sections.repair_procedure: Blend out the loss with an abrasive pad to a smooth dish with a length to depth ratio of at least twenty to one, and blend the edges. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the blended area. Where the cut-back and splice is required, cut the foot back to the nearest sound station square to the frame web, using a hand tool. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A ROTARY TOOL AT THE FOOT RADIUS. Install the splice from the lower frame cleat assembly D5331118141717 and the outboard shear tie sub-assembly D5331119974905, and add the forward frame doubler RO920514-03 across the joint. Ream the fastener holes and do an eddy current inspection of each. Fasten the splice with tension head bolts AGS713311K3 and solid rivets AGS120161-72 to the pitch and edge distance on repair drawing RD-53-31-11-002. Apply the chromate-free primer to every new surface and re-protect the whole foot. Restore the interrupted seal land where the aircraft standard has one.
sections.inspection_requirements: A blend-out repair is not life limited but requires a repeat ultrasonic thickness measurement of the blended area at every second corrosion inspection. A spliced repair is life limited to 20 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment and requires a repeat eddy current inspection of the splice fastener rows every 5 000 flight cycles. Any new indication inside the splice boundary makes the repair invalid. Report every spliced repair to Aeralis with the grid record so that the fleet corrosion model stays current.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Material loss up to 12 per cent of nominal thickness, not extending into the foot radius, not closer than 20 mm to a fastener centre, and at no more than three consecutive frame stations.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two staggered rows of 24 bolts AGS713311K3 at 22 mm pitch and 16 mm edge distance, closed out with 64 rivets AGS120161-72 on the doubler perimeter
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Blend-out is not life limited. Spliced renewal is life limited to 20 000 flight cycles with a repeat eddy current inspection every 5 000 flight cycles.

title: Aft Fuselage Frame Foot — Material Loss Blend-Out and Spliced Renewal

issue.reason: The repair now states what becomes of a spliced foot when the frame foot renewal standard is embodied over it, and requires the splice to be surveyed and closed out before the renewal is planned.

A splice left in place under the renewal is not an approved configuration and no inspection can be written for it.
